coverage.examinedBoundaries: Codex composer state/footer and annotation contexts; Memex Reader→ConversationComposer→AcpComposerView plus attachment/catalog/context helpers.
Codex queued-message-list and caller; Memex queue view, LiveConversation state machine, recovery view and existing tests.
Codex completed plan selection, editable/read-only panel, child summary/details, native fork service; Memex Work projection, history UI/store/runtime and child resume boundaries.
Codex pending request dispatcher, question picker, specialized permissions/review and elicitation; Memex pending projection/UI and exact Codex transport request/reply handling.
Codex local turn grouping, MCP tool result, find dispatch/history hydration; Memex Reader, NSTableView transcript, raw/structured tool content, rich blocks, literal paged find and outline.

findings.userWorkflow: Compose with files/images and refer to another chat or local command.
findings.comparatorState: Reachable composer context model carries image/file/pasted-text/selection/MCP/annotation attachment types.
findings.memexState: Native composer has file chooser, image/file paste/drop, file/chat mentions, slash commands, prompt stash and recall; captured contents are immutable and provider validated.

evidence.claim: Composer state has typed context collections.
Reachable native composer wires attachments, mentions, queue and steer.
Prompt stash, recall, mentions and commands are exposed.
Chat excerpt and file mentions enter attached context.
Captured contents become real blocks and enforce capability/size limits.

findings.implication: The ordinary context-composition workflow is already implemented. Richer structured contexts are assessed separately.
findings.recommendation: Retain existing composer; do not label attachments or mentions missing.
findings.caveats: Provider capability and live account availability were not exercised.

findings.userWorkflow: Attach comments tied to an image region or response passage, then edit/navigate them.
findings.comparatorState: Composer renders response annotations and image/diff/browser comment attachment collections with edit/navigation/removal callbacks.
findings.memexState: Memex provides text/image/file context and source labels; native composer and attachment APIs do not model response annotation identities or image comment drafts.

evidence.claim: Composer context UI exposes annotation edit and navigation callbacks.
Queued messages retain image comment collections and annotation counts.
Memex attachment UI maps only title/path/id and removal.
Native capture boundary stores generic text or image blocks, not editable annotation structures.

findings.implication: Users can supply the underlying text or screenshot, but cannot preserve and revise Codex-style contextual annotations in the composer.
findings.recommendation: Add annotation identity/location only for concrete supported Memex source surfaces; preserve current immutable capture behavior.
findings.caveats: Bounded absence: native ConversationComposer, ConversationPromptContext, ConversationAttachment and their public context item mapping. This does not claim no selection capture: terminal/browser selections have existing capture paths.

findings.userWorkflow: Record a prompt, transcribe it, and retry or recover recorded audio.
findings.comparatorState: Shared local composer footer accepts dictation controls; implementation has audio history read/retry/download and transcription.
findings.memexState: Native Memex composer and SQACPUI input surface expose text, mentions, file/image context and send/stop; no app-owned recording/transcription flow is wired.

evidence.claim: Local composer footer receives dictation state and controls.
Dictation history retry reads audio and transcribes it.
Full composer input/callback inventory contains no dictation integration.
Shared native composer types and implementation inspected; no dictation/speech recording APIs found.

findings.implication: System text-field dictation is different from an integrated recording/retry workflow.
findings.recommendation: Consider a dedicated native dictation path if voice input is a product goal.
findings.caveats: Codex dictation is feature/platform/service dependent; installed source proves integration, not that this account currently has it. No claim is made that macOS system dictation cannot type into Memex.

findings.userWorkflow: Compose during a run; choose queue or steer; edit/reorder pending work and stop safely.
findings.comparatorState: Reachable queue has reorder, edit, delete, steer, default queue/steer toggle and pause after interruption.
findings.memexState: Same core operations exist in ConversationQueueView and LiveConversation, including persisted queue and explicit pause/resume.

evidence.claim: Queue pauses and can resume after interruption.
Send-now action steers without interrupting.
Edit, move earlier/later, promote, remove and pause/resume are reachable.
Queue persists, checks capability, and dispatches prompt versus steer.
Existing tests cover persistence, stop settlement, steering identity and uncertain recovery; inspected, not run.

findings.implication: This is substantial current parity, with provider support checked before live steering.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the current queue state machine and tests; focus any polish on interaction details.
findings.caveats: Codex uses drag reorder; Memex exposes explicit earlier/later commands. Memex steering is gated by snapshot.canSteer and request/settings state.

findings.userWorkflow: Turn an already composed queued follow-up into a separate side chat.
findings.comparatorState: Queue action Open in side chat is supplied conditionally by the composer callback.
findings.memexState: Queue action inventory supports edit/reorder/steer/send/remove/pause, but has no branch/side-chat action.

evidence.claim: Queue menu optionally starts a queued message as a side chat.
Caller gates this action; it is not universal.
Complete native queue menu has no side-chat operation.

findings.implication: Memex users must manually move that prompt to a new conversation.
findings.recommendation: If adopting side chats, reuse queue attachment identity and perform a reviewed transfer rather than duplicate dispatch.
findings.caveats: Codex gate oc was not resolved to live entitlement; record as gated shipped source, not observed universal availability.

findings.userWorkflow: Recover a disconnected send without accidentally submitting it twice.
findings.comparatorState: Queue distinguishes sending/pending/outcome-unknown; warns to check conversation before deleting an unconfirmed message.
findings.memexState: Memex holds uncertain prompts and queue, preserves drafts and exposes reconnect/inspection; never auto-replays unconfirmed commands.

evidence.symbol: Delivery could not be confirmed. Check the conversation before deleting this saved message
evidence.claim: User-facing unknown-outcome state.
Distinct archive, authentication, uncertain delivery and reconnect states.
Explicit pending-prompt reconciliation.
Existing no-replay regression test.

findings.implication: Do not count recovery as absent; Memex deliberately makes uncertainty visible.
findings.recommendation: Keep recovery messages and provider identity checks.
findings.caveats: Provider capability and live account availability were not exercised.

findings.userWorkflow: Open the full generated plan, edit it in a file editor, then use the revised plan.
findings.comparatorState: Completed plan text can open an editable PLAN.md under the host Codex home; saves existing edits and falls back to a read-only panel when file writing is unavailable.
findings.memexState: Memex projects structured plan steps from update_plan/TodoWrite/native plan arrays and offers Refine/Implement/Implement in new conversation. Markdown plan text can be shown as tool detail, but does not become an editable plan document.

evidence.claim: Completed plan text is selected from conversation items.
Thread summary opens selected plan.
Plan panel creates/opens editable file with conflict and save handling; fallback read-only.
Only structured steps become the plan summary.
Refine/Implement buttons attach step text to a draft.
Markdown text is retained in details; structured payload is derived from arrays.

findings.implication: Planning exists, but document-oriented planning and direct editing are not equivalent to the step summary.
findings.recommendation: Preserve full plan identity/text and add an editable plan view with save/implementation provenance.
findings.caveats: Editable Codex plan requires workspaceFiles.write and a supported host. Do not claim the existing Memex planning mode or implementation actions are missing.

findings.userWorkflow: Inspect active/completed children and their model/effort without losing the parent.
findings.comparatorState: Dedicated subagent panel splits active/done and opens selected child details including model/reasoning; local thread summary links into it.
findings.memexState: Memex derives child identity/prompt/status/parent, offers Open and Parent for indexed sessions, and displays unavailable status honestly. It has no dedicated active/done side panel or per-child model/effort fields in this view.

evidence.claim: Active/completed sections in a dedicated panel.
Child detail header shows model and effort.
Memex child summary data consists of id, prompt, status, parentID.
Open/Parent require matching indexed child sessions.
Standalone resume of subagents is disallowed; parent is the control surface.

findings.implication: Child work is visible today, but navigation and metadata presentation are shallower.
findings.recommendation: Extend the existing child summary using authoritative provider state; avoid inferring completion from tool return.
findings.caveats: Codex child interactivity is explicitly canInteract-gated. No claim of universal direct child messaging is made. Memex parent-owned transport can handle child requests.

findings.capability: Native fork, rewind and context branch
findings.userWorkflow: Branch at a selected turn or reuse prior context in another conversation.
findings.comparatorState: Fork service retains history, supports same-directory and asynchronous worktree fork, and distinguishes incomplete setup.
findings.memexState: Memex has native fork/rewind at valid boundaries, context branch/provider transition/new worktree, persisted relationships and recovery journal.

evidence.claim: Same-directory native fork.
Asynchronous worktree fork retains working-tree starting state.
Reachable branch/fork/rewind actions and recovery notice.
Context branch can request new worktree; native mutation records relationship.
Native fork/revert requires compatibility and verifies chosen cutoff.

findings.implication: History operations are not a Memex gap, though native worktree fork and context-with-worktree are distinct workflows.
findings.recommendation: Keep the explicit native-history versus captured-context distinction.
findings.caveats: Parity is at workflow family level. Memex native mutation requires idle state, empty queue and provider capability; this is not a claim that its context branch is an identical native-history worktree fork.

findings.userWorkflow: Answer multiple pending choice/freeform/secret questions without losing drafts.
findings.comparatorState: Question picker supports selected options, freeform Other, multi-select and secret fields; request panel dispatches userInput.
findings.memexState: Memex projects native question identity/choice values/multiselect/secret flags; retains drafts while navigating; answers can include captured UTF-8 files.

evidence.claim: Pending-request dispatcher exposes structured questions.
Question picker handles multi-selection and secret input.
Back/Next retains per-question drafts; submission preserves exact choice values and text context.
Answers accumulate by native question ID until the group can respond.

findings.implication: Ordinary questions already have a substantive native implementation.
findings.recommendation: Retain grouped reply identity and draft preservation.
findings.caveats: This does not imply parity for MCP JSON-schema elicitation or Codex async/autoresolved questions; those use different protocols.

findings.userWorkflow: Fill an MCP server requested form and return the entered structured content.
findings.comparatorState: MCP elicitation dispatcher recognizes formElicitation/openaiForm/legacyOpenAIForm and opens a dedicated form component.
findings.memexState: Codex transport maps mcpServer/elicitation/request to generic approval options and respondPermission always sends content null, including accept.

evidence.claim: Dedicated form elicitation dispatch, separate from simple approvals.
Elicitation is projected as approval, not a schema-backed question form.
Accepted response explicitly contains NSNull content.
Memex supplies only title/detail/options to approval UI.

findings.implication: A form that requires entered values cannot be completed correctly through this path; clicking Allow does not supply them.
findings.recommendation: Add a typed elicitation form/reply path or explicitly reject unsupported required forms instead of offering a misleading empty accept.
findings.caveats: Source-proven limitation of Memex Codex transport, not a claim that every MCP elicitation requires content or that every ACP provider has the same behavior.

findings.capability: Policy amendment and reviewer detail UI
findings.userWorkflow: Approve a reusable command/network rule and inspect automatic review rationale.
findings.comparatorState: Approval panel exposes exec/network policy amendments; automatic-review details show denied/high-risk rationale and review state.
findings.memexState: Generic Memex approval panel supports allow once/session/deny and raw request detail. Codex adapter filters command decisions to string accept/acceptForSession, and its notification switch lacks dedicated guardian review start/completion projection.

evidence.claim: Native network policy amendment action.
Exec amendment is part of specialized approval UI.

evidence.symbol: Requires explicit authorization because this action is considered high risk
evidence.claim: Review detail presentation distinguishes high risk denials.
Only accept, session, decline/cancel decisions are surfaced/serialized.
Generic guardianWarning is handled; dedicated review lifecycle is not projected here.
UI projection carries generic title, raw detail and options.

findings.implication: Approval works, but users do not get the same scoped rule controls or review explanation UI.
findings.recommendation: Project only supported typed decisions and review events; keep unknown data inspectable.
findings.caveats: Memex already configures auto_review for noninteractive approval policy. The gap is specialized decision/presentation, not lack of auto-review backend selection.

findings.capability: Core readable transcript, search and navigation
findings.userWorkflow: Read Markdown/tool output, inspect raw data, find a message and branch from history.
findings.comparatorState: Local turn renderer groups user/assistant/activity entries; thread find command and history search hydration exist.
findings.memexState: Memex native transcript provides Markdown tables/code/links/images, structured tool output with raw disclosure, completed-work folding, paginated find and prompt outline.

evidence.claim: Local turn rendering separates user content from activity groups.
Native find command is dispatched.
History search results can be hydrated.
Reachable reader includes recovery, work view and find state.
Cancellable paged whole-conversation literal find.
Completed routine work folds while failures remain visible.
Native Markdown code, quotes, headings, lists and tables.
Raw tool content remains inspectable beside structured rendering.

findings.implication: A broad missing-transcript/search claim would be inaccurate.
findings.recommendation: Retain native rendering and provenance; extend only concrete richer content types.
findings.caveats: Source inspection does not measure runtime performance or accessibility quality. Codex find reachability was traced through command dispatch/hydration, not exercised. Memex literal find is not regex search.

findings.userWorkflow: Use an interactive app returned by a tool directly from its conversation result.
findings.comparatorState: Local turn renderer passes renderMcpApps into tool activity; MCP tool component resolves app metadata/resource, open/reopen widget activity, and side-panel app representation.
findings.memexState: Runtime has AgentMcpAppProjection, but native Memex renderer/projection does not consume mcpApp; its rich-content cases cover text/code/images/attachments and tool results are generic.

evidence.claim: Local thread turn forwards MCP app rendering controls.
Tool result offers app opening/open/error/reopen states.
App resource and metadata are resolved for MCP result.
Underlying runtime retains typed MCP app projection.
Reachable native reader uses SourceContent and ToolContentRenderer.
Complete native rich block inventory has no interactive app host.
Typed media/text/tool blocks do not create MCP app hosts.

findings.implication: Runtime protocol support alone does not make interactive tool apps usable inside Memex.
findings.recommendation: Wire typed runtime app metadata to a native host with scoped messaging and restore behavior, retaining generic fallback.
findings.caveats: Absence boundary: searched apps/macos/Sources/Memex and MemexExecutionHostCore for mcpApp/MCPApp/McpApp/uiResource; no consumers, then traced Reader→TranscriptController→RichContentView/ToolContentRenderer. Codex rendering remains metadata/feature gated; not every tool result is an app.

unresolved: All findings are source inspection. No app launch, UI interaction, provider prompts, tests, or runtime observations were performed.
Live feature flags/account entitlements for Codex dictation, queue-to-side-chat, editable plan on each host, MCP app embedding and child interactivity were not queried.
Advanced math/Mermaid/audio/video rendering equivalence was not claimed: libraries coexist with ChatGPT assets and need additional route-specific tracing before a Codex claim.
Codex async/automatic question-resolution behavior is present in source but not compared as ordinary requestUserInput parity; provider/version availability requires a separate bounded check.
No universal ACP-provider claims: concrete elicitation/policy gaps apply to the traced Codex transport; other provider capabilities can differ.
